```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day paying-customer goal favors A's buying motion. A sells self-serve through the Shopify App Store at $12-$19/month, with ads starting at $5/day. A single merchant can install and pay with no procurement step. B's own brief concedes that municipal procurement (RFPs, insurance certificates, cooperative-purchasing vetting) is slow and a poor fit for a fast build-and-sell cycle.",
    "A has sourced evidence that merchants pay for this category. AltText.ai has 141 reviews at 4.5 stars on paid tiers, and several live competitors charge $12-$130/month. That shows willingness to pay at a price a solo operator can collect quickly.",
    "B's urgency is weakening. The deadlines were extended to April 2027 and April 2028, and the brief flags that further delays or lax enforcement could erode willingness to pay. A's pain (procrastinating on descriptions, catalog upkeep) does not depend on a regulatory date.",
    "B carries liability risk that is hard for a solo, uninsured operator. Its pricing power sits in legally defensible compliance documentation, and A has no comparable exposure.",
    "A's weaknesses are serious, but they threaten scale and retention more than a first sale. Shopify Magic covers basic descriptions for free, the category is saturated, and the need may be one-time per catalog. The brief also notes Shopify Magic does not handle alt text, images, or bulk editing, which leaves a reachable paid wedge.",
    "A's own evidence has a weak spot. The ADA settlement figures ($25k-$75k) and the '77% of lawsuits' statistic come from vendor marketing blogs, so the alt-text urgency claim deserves a discount."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence rests on two quotes from a single news article about one county, Cole County, MO. That county has already bought a competitor's tool for $7,000, so it is not a prospect. One of the quotes describes removing information from the website as the compliance strategy, which points toward avoiding spending rather than paying a new vendor. The acquisition-channel cost is also weak: the booth figures come from a 2015 NLC prospectus, and the one current data point says state-league booths are already sold out.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B has stronger sourced evidence of real municipal spending (the $7,000 and $2,510 figures). A's market is saturated and partly undercut by free Shopify Magic. The deciding factor is the 90-day constraint: self-serve App Store sales fit a solo operator far better than municipal procurement. A longer horizon could flip the verdict."
}
```
